messages:
james (Customer): Hi team — customer on EU plan asking for a few compliance items asap: full sub-processor list for EU data, an export of audit logs for the past 13 months, and evidence that user data for tenant `org-42` was deleted after retention period. They also asked how our KMS/HSM handles customer-derived keys. They need this for a regulator review by EOW.
anna (Support): Thanks James — can you share the customer org ID (confirmed: org-42) and the exact time window they want for the audit log export? Also are they asking for object-level deletion proofs or account-level data erasure certs?
james (Customer): Window: 2024-01-01 to 2025-01-31. They want both: audit trails for access + deletion evidence that the artifacts were removed from primary and backup storage. Regulator wants chain-of-custody.
anna (Support): Got it. Escalating to Security & Privacy. tagging @raj @olivia. I'll kick off a request ticket for log export and tell the customer expected ETA ~48h.
support-bot: New incident export request created: #INC-2025-334. ETA: 48 hours. Uploaded artifacts will be stored in a secure S3 export and notification sent when ready.
raj (Security): Quick notes — for KMS: we use customer-specific keys in our KMS integration for Private deployments; for Hosted, keys are managed by Redwood by default unless customer has a BYOK contract. HSM-backed keys are available for enterprise customers. We sign exports with our service key and can provide key fingerprints. For org-42, do we have BYOK/HSM on contract? If not, deletion proofs will reference server-side keys.
olivia (Privacy): On roles: Redwood is a processor under the DPA; the customer is the controller. We can supply sub-processor list and standard deletion certificates. For backups — we have an immutable retention window but can provide attestations showing when the data was rendered unrecoverable and which storage tiers were affected.
anna (Support): raj — can you provide the export steps & commands so I can include in the ticket? Also need the sub-processor doc link for the customer.
raj (Security): Steps to generate audit export (internal runbook, summary):

1) Run admin export tool against org `org-42`:

```
redwood-admin exports create --org org-42 --from 2024-01-01 --to 2025-01-31 --type audit,access
```

2) Tool collects logs, redacts ephemeral tokens, bundles and signs with service key, uploads to secure S3 (path: s3://redwood-exports/INC-2025-334/org-42-20240101-20250131.tar.gz)

3) Generate deletion certificate for objects listed in deletion manifest:

```
redwood-admin delete-manifest attest --org org-42 --manifest s3://redwood-manifests/org-42/deletions-2025.json
```

4) If customer has BYOK/HSM, note in cert: `key_management: BYOK/HSM` and include key fingerprint.

I can run step 1-3 if support authorizes. ETA ~6-12h for exports + additional time for deletion attestations.

Also: sub-processor list here: https://redwood-inference.example.com/legal/subprocessors (public doc). Provide latest snapshot in the export.

anna (Support): Authorizing now. Raj — please proceed with steps 1-3. Olivia — can you prep a short deletion attestation template we can fill for backups and cold-tier objects? The customer will want it signed.
olivia (Privacy): I will prepare template. Important to note: the attestation will state that backup copies are either expired and cryptographically shredded or rotated beyond recovery in accordance with our retention policy. We will include retention policy version and timestamp.
raj (Security): Running export now. Quick heads up: we hit an API error earlier this week for org exports tied to a high-latency S3 endpoint — if export stalls, I will switch to fallback region endpoint and re-run. If anyone sees `503` or `x-retry-after` failures in the logs, ping me.
anna (Support): Thanks. James, I'll update the customer: export started, expected secure link later today if no fallback needed. Will include the sub-processor snapshot and deletion attestation once ready.
james (Customer): Appreciate it. One more Q: for the KMS/HSM line item — can you confirm whether keys for hosted customers are backed by HSM or software KMS? They need to know for the regulator.
raj (Security): For hosted (default) we use cloud KMS (software-backed) with a HSM-protected root in the provider. For enterprise Private, customers can bring HSM-backed keys (BYOK with HSM). I will include a short FAQ blurb in the export explaining differences and provide the key fingerprint snippet for org-42 if BYOK is present.
anna (Support): Update: export finished and uploaded to s3://redwood-exports/INC-2025-334/org-42-20240101-20250131.tar.gz. Sharing secure download link via ticket (pre-signed URL). Deletion attestation draft attached to the ticket (olivia to sign).
olivia (Privacy): Draft attestation uploaded to ticket. It states data deletion completed for objects listed and describes backup non-recoverability timeline. I added the retention policy id: rp-v3.2 and timestamped evidence for when backups expired.
raj (Security): I included KMS key fingerprint: SHA256:AB:12:CD:34:EF:56:78:90:AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF:00:11:22:33:44:55:66:77:88:99:00:AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF:00:11

Also noted no BYOK contract on file for org-42 — so hosted keys only.
anna (Support): Sent customer the ticket update with link and attachments. Requested ack from regulator contact and offered 1:1 call to walk through artifacts. Marking thread resolved after customer confirms.
james (Customer): Confirmed receipt; regulator scheduled call tomorrow. Thank you all :pray:

anna (Support): Closing internal thread but keeping incident #INC-2025-334 open until regulator confirms. :thumbsup:
